items.title: requires-python specification not correctly resolved
items.reason: Historical bug in the same `uv lock` intersection path: a valid `!=` hole became contradictory bounds. The closed case used one exact exclusion, not two consecutive wildcard exclusions.

items.title: Fix handling of != intersections in `requires-python`
items.reason: The fix for astral-sh/uv#7862 changed `RequiresPython::intersection` to prevent exclusions from being lost or converted into contradictory bounds.

items.title: Add gap-preserving range-to-PEP 440 routine
items.reason: This follow-up introduced the current conversion routine. It preserves exact and single-minor holes but explicitly drops unsupported wider gaps, which closely explains the consecutive-wildcard case.

items.title: `project.requires-python` not handled correctly
items.reason: Adjacent context confirming `!=X.Y.*` is the recommended syntax for skipping one minor. Unlike the new report, it does not involve two consecutive exclusions.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and all pull request states using the exact specifiers, `requires-python`, `uv.lock`, ignored/simplified exclusions, wildcard exclusions, unsupported gaps, non-contiguous Python support, range normalization/intersection, and `[tool.uv].environments`. Fix-oriented searches followed astral-sh/uv#7862 through astral-sh/uv#7897 and astral-sh/uv#8060. astral-sh/uv#6031 was ruled out because it concerns `uv pip compile --universal` not reading project bounds; astral-sh/uv#6064 and astral-sh/uv#6176 concern resolver forks and markers; astral-sh/uv#15995 concerns `pylock.toml` interpreter-derived bounds.

type_reason: The valid PEP 440 constraint is widened, changing the supported Python versions. Source confirms workspace intersection reconstructs specifiers from ranges and drops unsupported gaps. Historical fixes covered exact and single-minor holes but not two consecutive wildcard exclusions, and no open tracker covers this case.
summary: This is an uncovered correctness case in exclusion-preserving `requires-python` normalization, closely related to the closed astral-sh/uv#7862 fix chain but not a duplicate.
draft_response: Thanks, this is a bug. The constraint is valid and `uv lock` should not widen it. This is in the same conversion path previously addressed by astral-sh/uv#7862, astral-sh/uv#7897, and astral-sh/uv#8060, but that work does not cover two consecutive wildcard exclusions: they become one wider gap that the current conversion drops. Keeping this issue open for that uncovered case is appropriate. Your `[tool.uv].environments` setting is a valid workaround; the next implementation step is an integration regression test for this exact constraint followed by preserving the gap during workspace `requires-python` intersection.
